target.statement: OmniISR improves mIoU over the output-layer-only baseline on the smallest semantic-segmentation benchmark (CamVid) in a single training mode, as reported in the main results table (e.g., the CL or FL mIoU cell for the DeepLabv3+/ResNet backbone).

compute.basis: No code is released, so an agent must rebuild the full OmniISR loss (CE + MI supervision + NE regularizer at multiple layers), the DeepLabv3+ segmentation pipeline, and the FL simulation loop from scratch, then train to convergence on segmentation data; even the smallest dataset demands many GPU-hours and full CPU training is impractical.

blockers: No code, configs, or hyperparameters released (release: none)
Requires training deep semantic-segmentation models (DeepLabv3+/TopFormer/SeaFormer), plus a multi-client federated simulation, all built from scratch
Convergence on segmentation data is GPU-bound; a normal CPU laptop cannot finish a faithful re-run of the protocol in a few hours
Detailed experimental tables are in the omitted middle pages, so exact target cell values/configs are not readable
title: OmniISR: A Unified Framework for Centralized and Federated Learning via Intermediate Supervision and Regularization
